requiredFindings.title: Synthetic one-finding-per-source timings are not a justified lower bound on real workload replay
locations: REPORT.md:70-88 (SM-9_lb workload table and F/outcome inference)
sized-replay-checks-r1.json (lowerBoundAssumption, inference and workload lower-bound labels)
requiredFindings.description: The lower-bound assumption asserts that real graphs carry at least one fact and one finding per analysed source and treats monotone medians of this synthetic graph family as replay-time monotonicity for real graphs. Neither premise is established. The closed generator deliberately selects an exists/file predicate and asserts exactly count findings; the measured evaluator emits a finding only when a selected rule predicate is true. Real findings need not occur once per source. Arbitrary graph topology, rule/predicate work, retained descriptors and bytes are also not ordered by source count or by this synthetic family's empirical medians.
evidence: prepare_packet.py:8 forces atom_override={op:exists, relation:file, minResolution:enumerated, filters:[]} and asserts len(findingIds)==count. That is a synthetic fixture choice, not a measured F/G3 output minimum.

At product 37581132, crates/evaluator/src/composition.rs:871-894 evaluates each selected rule predicate and skips finding emission at :887-888 unless its value is true. There is no one-finding-per-source invariant; zero emitted findings are lawful.

The 208-source retained packet contains 208 fact, 208 finding and 208 finding-fingerprint objects. No embedding or work-dominance proof relates these artificial finding/proof objects to the real workload's retained graph.

The measured fourteen-size synthetic medians are monotone, but this proves only a property of those observations, not a replay-time lower bound over different real graphs or unmeasured current-head replay.

All seven measured samples exceed 2 s for the nine listed synthetic sizing scenarios. Without a valid SM-9 lower bound, those observations do not establish F>2 s or the failure of outcome (A) for the corresponding real workloads.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Preserve the closed generators, images, retained refusal and raw series. Either relabel these as workload-sized synthetic replay/scaling scenarios and remove the SM-9_lb/lower-bound and real-workload F/outcome implications from the report, audit and derived labels, or supply an independently reviewable conservative sizing/work-dominance justification tied to the actual selected workload graph and replay boundary. Merely declaring a lead assumption or citing monotone synthetic medians is insufficient. Until justified, no workload-level lower-bound failure is established and outcome (A) remains unestablished for all 14 rows.
